Even better in modern Excel: =XLOOKUP($A2,Prices!$A$2:$A$900,Prices!$D$2:$D$900,"not found") — it defaults to exact match, doesn't need a column number, and lets you set a fallback value.

results.what_changed: Wrapped the calculation in IF so that when the previous-year value is empty or zero, the cell stays blank instead of showing an error.

results.whats_broken: The comparison operator is written as '=>' instead of '>='.
results.why: In Excel, the greater-than-or-equal-to operator must be written as '>=' (greater-than sign first, then equals). Writing '=>' is not recognized as a valid operator, so Excel will either show an error or treat it as text, causing the formula to fail. This is a simple typo that is easy to fix.
results.what_changed: Changed '=>' to '>=' so the comparison works correctly.
